name: anim_create
title: anim.create
description:
Create an animation (group + optional direction) with empty frames of equal duration.

(group, direction) must be unique. Names: lower-case a-z 0-9 _ - up to 48 characters; omit direction for an undirected animation. Frames start empty: pose them with rig_set_pose, draw into them, or add more with frame_add. Use loop "once" for a one-shot such as a jump: in a "loop" the keys interpolate across the wrap, from the last frame to the first. For a flipped copy of a side animation use rig_mirror_animation.

Edit: one undo step. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (A 4-frame side run loop at 100 ms): {"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","group":"run","direction":"side","frames":4}

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_create.

durationMs.description: Duration of every frame in ms (default 100).

angleQuantum.description: Rig angle quantum, deg (a multiple of 0.25 that divides 360; default 1).

animation.description: Animation id.

name: anim_update
title: anim.update
description:
Rename an animation (group, direction), set its loop mode, angle quantum or post-passes.

(group, direction) must stay unique. Renaming the group of a source animation renames its mirrors too; a mirror's group cannot change on its own. Loop, angleQuantum and postPasses belong to the source: a mirror has none. null clears direction, angleQuantum or postPasses. The loop mode changes how keys interpolate at the ends: "loop" wraps from the last frame to the first, "once" and "pingpong" hold. Frame durations, markers, events: frame_set_meta.

Edit: one undo step. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (Make the hero idle a ping-pong): {"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","animation":{"group":"default"},"loop":"pingpong"}

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_create.

animation.description: Animation: {"group": "run", "direction": "side"} ({"group": "idle"} for an undirected one) or {"id": "anm_..."}.

direction.description: New direction; null makes it undirected.

angleQuantum.description: Rig angle quantum, deg (multiple of 0.25 dividing 360); null restores the default.

postPasses.description: Post-passes after the rig render: {removeOrphans: {}, outline: {color: [r,g,b,a], outsideOnly?, corners?}}; null removes them.

animation.description: Animation id.

changed.description: Fields that changed; empty when nothing did.

mirrors.description: Labels of the mirror animations renamed with it.

name: cel_link
title: cel.link
description:
Link a layer's cel to another frame's cel (mode "link"), make a linked cel independent ("unlink"), or link all identical cels ("linkIdentical").

A linked cel shows the same pixels as its target; links cross animations, one hop (a link to a link goes to its target). "link": animation, frame (the cel that becomes the link), source.frame (source.animation defaults to animation). "unlink" copies the pixels into the cel. "linkIdentical" links, per layer, every cel with identical pixels, offset and opacity to the first in document order. Pixel layers only: part layers have no cels.

Edit: one undo step. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (Link the hero layer cels that have identical pixels): {"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","layer":"body","mode":"linkIdentical"}

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_create.

animation.description: link/unlink: animation of the cel. linkIdentical: limits the scan (default: all).

source.description: link: the frame whose cel is shown.

animation.description: Animation of the source frame (default: animation).

changed.description: Cels that were linked or unlinked (0 for a no-op).

imagesDeleted.description: Images that nothing used any more.

name: doc_create
title: doc.create
description:
Create a new empty RGBA document (no layers, no animations) and open it. Save it with doc_save.

The origin defaults to the bottom-centre pixel of the canvas (where the feet go). For a sprite sheet make the canvas the size of one cell. Import art with import_file, apply a skeleton with rig_apply_template, add animations with anim_create. Use doc_set_color_mode for indexed colour. Nothing is on disk until doc_save with a path.

File I/O. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (A 48x48 canvas): {"name":"hero","width":48,"height":48}

origin.description: Origin pixel on the canvas, int px (default: bottom-centre).

idSeed.description: Seed of the id generator (default: derived from the host clock).

doc.description: Document id for the other ops.

name: doc_open
title: doc.open
description:
Open a .pxf file and return its document id, which every other op takes as "doc".

Opening a file that is already open returns the same id (alreadyOpen: true) without re-reading it. Returns the id only: read layers, rig and animations with doc_summary next.

File I/O. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (Open the synthetic hero): {"path":"/work/hero.pxf"}

path.description: Path of the .pxf file (absolute, inside the workspace roots).

doc.description: Document id for the other ops.

alreadyOpen.description: True when the file was open already.

warnings.description: Problems found while reading (e.g. a dropped render cache).

name: redo
title: doc.redo
description:
Redo the newest undone change of the document (one history entry).

Re-applies the entry that the last undo reverted. A new change clears the redo entries. Nothing to redo is not an error: redone is false.

Moves through the history, adds no undo step. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (Redo on a fresh open (nothing to redo)): {"doc":"doc_g1ed5q"}

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_create.

redone.description: True when an entry was re-applied; false when there was nothing to redo.

label.description: Label of the re-applied entry (for example "AI: rig.setPose"); null when nothing was redone.

name: doc_save
title: doc.save
description:
Save the document to its .pxf file, or to a new path (first save, save as).

Nothing reaches disk before this call. With doc alone it saves to the file the document came from; a document from doc_create needs path (absolute, inside the workspace roots). Writes a temp file and renames it over the target, so a crash never leaves a torn file. A new path takes the document's lock first (DOC_LOCKED if another process owns it). An existing file at a new path is refused unless overwrite is true. An unchanged document writes nothing, unless its file lacks a current render cache or has an older schema version.

File I/O. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (Save the hero under a new name): {"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","path":"/work/hero-v2.pxf"}

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_create.

path.description: Target .pxf path (absolute, inside the workspace roots). Default: the current path.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file at a new path (default false).

wrote.description: False when the file was already what this save would write and nothing was written.

bytes.description: Size of the file written, bytes (0 when nothing was written).

name: doc_set_color_mode
title: doc.setColorMode
description:
Switch the document between "rgba" and "indexed" pixels, and/or lock it to its palette.

Converting is exact: to "indexed" every colour must be an entry of the active palette (the first alpha-0 entry is the transparent index), else the call is refused and nothing changes; to "rgba" indices resolve through the palette. Both need an active palette. The lock does not recolour: run lint next (palette.offPalette judges the render).

Edit: one undo step. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (Lock a document that has a palette to it): {"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","paletteLocked":true}

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_create.

paletteLocked.description: Lock colours to the active palette (default: unchanged).

name: doc_summary
title: doc.summary
description:
Summarise an open document: canvas, palette, layers, rig (bones, parts, views) and animations.

Names in the result (bones, parts, layers, animation group/direction) are what the other tools take as references. It shows no rest angles and no pose keys: for pivots and tips as numbers use render_frame with bones: true.

Read-only. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (Summarise the hero): {"doc":"doc_g1ed5q"}

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_create.
Document id.

path.description: Backing file, null for an unsaved document.

version.description: Runtime version: +1 per change, undo and redo.

dirty.description: Changed (or undone/redone) since it was opened or last saved.

origin.description: Anchor pixel shared with the engine (mirroring flips about origin.x).

palette.description: The active palette, null when there is none.

path.description: Names from the root, joined by "/".

layers.description: Every layer, depth first, bottom to top.

name.description: Part-layer name: how ops address the part.

rig.description: Null when the document has no rig.

frames.description: Frame count (the source animation for a mirror).

mirrorOf.description: Label of the source animation of a mirror.

name: undo
title: doc.undo
description:
Undo the newest applied change of the document (one history entry).

Reverts the last applied history entry, whatever tool made it. Nothing to undo is not an error: undone is false. Re-apply with redo.

Moves through the history, adds no undo step. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (Undo the last change of the hero (nothing to undo on a fresh open)): {"doc":"doc_g1ed5q"}

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_create.

undone.description: True when an entry was reverted; false when there was nothing to undo.

label.description: Label of the reverted entry (for example "AI: rig.setPose"); null when nothing was undone.

name: frame_add
title: frame.add
description:
Insert an empty frame before or after a frame; the new frame gets no bone or part keys.

The new frame has no keys, so bones and parts interpolate into it from the neighbouring keys. Cels and overrides are not copied (frame_duplicate copies them). Set its keys with rig_set_pose.

Edit: one undo step. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (Add an empty frame after frame 0 of the hero): {"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","animation":{"group":"default"},"frame":0}

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_create.

animation.description: Animation: {"group": "run", "direction": "side"} ({"group": "idle"} for an undirected one) or {"id": "anm_..."}.

frame.description: Reference frame: the new frame goes next to it.

position.description: "after" (default) inserts behind the reference frame, "before" in front of it.

durationMs.description: Duration of the new frame in ms (default: the reference frame duration).

frameIndex.description: Index of the new frame in the animation.

frames.description: Frame count of the animation afterwards.

name: frame_delete
title: frame.delete
description:
Delete one frame with its bone and part keys, cels and overrides; the last frame cannot go.

Links to the frame's cels are materialised first: the other linked frames keep their picture as their own copy. Images nothing references any more are removed. Later frames move down one index. An animation keeps at least one frame.

Edit: one undo step. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (Delete frame 1 of the hero (add a second frame first; the hero has one)): {"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","animation":{"group":"default"},"frame":1}

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_create.

animation.description: Animation: {"group": "run", "direction": "side"} ({"group": "idle"} for an undirected one) or {"id": "anm_..."}.

frames.description: Frame count of the animation afterwards.

name: frame_duplicate
title: frame.duplicate
description:
Duplicate one frame; the copy goes right after it, with linked cels and copied keys.

Cels of the copy link to the source frame (edit one, both change). Bone keys, part keys, markers, events, root motion, duration and overrides are copied, so the copy starts from the same pose: change it with rig_set_pose.

Edit: one undo step. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (Duplicate frame 0 of the hero): {"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","animation":{"group":"default"},"frame":0}

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_create.

animation.description: Animation: {"group": "run", "direction": "side"} ({"group": "idle"} for an undirected one) or {"id": "anm_..."}.

frameIndex.description: Index of the new frame (source index + 1).

frames.description: Frame count of the animation afterwards.

name: frame_set_meta
title: frame.setMeta
description:
Set one frame's duration (ms), markers (name -> int px), events (names) and root motion (int px).

Only the fields you give change, on this one frame. markers merge by name (null removes one); events replace the whole list; rootMotion is the move the game applies when this frame plays (int px, y down). New marker and event names join the document's markerDefs / eventDefs. Mirror animations have no frames: edit the source.

Edit: one undo step. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (Hold the hero frame 200 ms and fire a footstep event): {"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","animation":{"group":"default"},"frame":0,"durationMs":200,"events":["footstep"]}

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_create.

animation.description: Animation: {"group": "run", "direction": "side"} ({"group": "idle"} for an undirected one) or {"id": "anm_..."}.

markers.description: Markers by name, canvas px (e.g. "hand_r": {"x": 30, "y": 20}); null removes one.

events.description: Event names fired on this frame; replaces the list.

rootMotion.description: Root motion of this frame, int px.

animation.description: "group/direction" of the animation.

changed.description: Fields that changed; empty when nothing did.

name: export
title: io.export
description:
Export animations as a spritesheet PNG plus a JSON description (Aseprite hash format).

Renders every frame like the game would see it (export layers only; rig, overrides and post-passes applied; mirrors flipped) and writes <name>.png and <name>.json side by side, atomically. layout "rows" puts one animation per row; "packed" fills a near-square grid. scale is an integer 1..16. The JSON lists a frame per cell with its duration, and one tag per animation. To look at art use render_contact_sheet instead; a scale 1 export of one animation is the base for override_import.

File I/O. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (Export the hero as a 2x sheet): {"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","path":"/work/out/hero.png","scale":2}

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_create.

path.description: Output PNG path (absolute, inside the workspace roots); the JSON goes beside it.

animations.description: Animations to export, in order (default: all).

items.description: Animation: {"group": "run", "direction": "side"} ({"group": "idle"} for an undirected one) or {"id": "anm_..."}.

exportOnly.description: Only layers with export: true (default true).

name: import_file
title: io.import
description:
Import a PNG spritesheet (cells per animation) or an .aseprite file into a document.

Spritesheet: animations maps cells to animations; repeated cells become linked cels; the cell's bottom-centre lands on the document origin. To keep the sheet as a reference, import the frame to cut again as its own animation and layer. Aseprite: run rig_apply_template first or part layers stay unbound; adds layers, tags (as animations) and the palette; the canvas must equal the document's.

File I/O. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (Cut row 0, columns 0 to 2 of a 64x64 sheet into move_gather at 12 fps): {"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","file":"/work/run.png","cell":[64,64],"animations":[{"group":"move_gather","cells":[{"row":0,"col":"0-2"}],"fps":12}]}

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_create.

file.description: Path of the file (absolute, inside the workspace roots).

cell.description: spritesheet: cell size [w, h] px (default: the whole image is one cell).

animations.description: spritesheet: the animations to cut (required for a spritesheet).

row.description: Row (0-based, row 0 on top), or a range "from-to".

cells.description: Cells in play order: [row, col], or {"row": 4, "col": "3-6"} for row 4, columns 3 to 6.

outlineFile.description: spritesheet: matching outline sheet, same size.

layerName.description: spritesheet: layer for the cels (default "body"; reused if it exists).

outlineLayerName.description: spritesheet: layer of the outline sheet (default "outline").

defaultDurationMs.description: spritesheet: frame duration when an animation gives none (default 100).

reimport.description: aseprite: update a file imported earlier instead of adding (default false).

view.description: aseprite: rig view for "part:" layers without #view (default: the first).

paletteName.description: aseprite: name of the imported palette.

frames.description: Frames created (re-import: frames in the file).

parts.description: aseprite: "part:" layers bound, updated (re-import) or left as pixel layers.

name: layer_update
title: layer.update
description:
Rename a layer, or set its visible flag, opacity (0..255) or export flag.

Only the fields you give change. Names are lower-case a-z 0-9 _ - up to 48 characters and unique among siblings; a part layer's name is the part's name and must be unique in the document. A reference layer is never exported. Hidden or non-exported layers are skipped by export, lint and rig_bake. To hide a part on some frames only, key visible with rig_set_pose.

Edit: one undo step. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (Hide the hero's head part from the editor render): {"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","layer":"head","visible":false}

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_create.

visible.description: Show or hide the layer in the editor render.

export.description: Include the layer in exports and bakes.

path.description: Name path from the root afterwards (e.g. "body/arm").

changed.description: Fields that changed; empty when nothing did.

name: lint
title: lint.run
description:
Lint the document: palette, orphan pixels, joint gaps, stale overrides, empty frames, clipping, holes.

Sorted by rule, then document order. Narrow with enable, disable, animations or skins. "error" means a broken invariant; fix warnings before delivery. pixels.clipped: part art cut off at the canvas edge. rig.partHole: 1 px holes in rotated parts. count 0 is not a visual pass (jointGap checks rest only): see render_contact_sheet.

Read-only. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (Lint the hero, joint and palette rules only): {"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","enable":["rig.jointGap","palette.offPalette"]}

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_create.

enable.description: Run only these rule ids (default: all).

disable.description: Skip these rule ids (applied after enable).

animations.description: Animations to render and check (default: all, in document order).

items.description: Animation: {"group": "run", "direction": "side"} ({"group": "idle"} for an undirected one) or {"id": "anm_..."}.

skins.description: Skin names to render for palette checks; "base" is the base colours (default: base, then every skin).

severity.description: "error" breaks an invariant, "warning" should be fixed, "info" may be intended.

location.description: Where the finding is; a rule fills the fields that apply.

data.description: Machine-readable details; keys per rule are in packages/lint/README.md.

name: override_import
title: override.import
description:
Import an edited PNG of a rig frame: the pixels that differ from the render become overrides.

Touch-up path: export the frame (export, scale 1, one animation), edit the PNG, import it. The PNG must be canvas-sized; it is compared with the exported render. Each changed stroke becomes a part override when one part owns it, else a final one, and survives re-posing. `newlyStale` lists earlier overrides it made stale: see override_list. Needs a rig; palette-locked and indexed documents only take palette colours.

File I/O. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (Import the touched-up frame 2 of the run animation): {"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","animation":{"group":"run","direction":"side"},"frame":2,"file":"/work/run-2-edited.png"}

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_create.

animation.description: Animation: {"group": "run", "direction": "side"} ({"group": "idle"} for an undirected one) or {"id": "anm_..."}.

file.description: The edited PNG (absolute, inside the workspace roots), canvas size, scale 1.

animation.description: "group/direction" of the animation edited.

changed.description: Pixels that differ from the render (0: nothing was written).

overrides.description: Ids of the overrides created, in order.

newlyStale.description: Ids of earlier overrides this import made stale (still applied).

name: override_list
title: override.list
description:
List overrides: stale ones (art under them changed) and ones that fail to render, apart.

Renders the frames that have overrides. "stale" overrides are still applied; decide with override_resolve (keep, rebase = accept the current art, discard). "errors" cannot be judged because their frame does not render (missing image, no view for the direction...): fix the rig first, they cannot be rebased until it renders. Part overrides of mirror animations are never rendered and not listed.

Read-only. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (List the hero overrides): {"doc":"doc_g1ed5q"}

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_create.

items.description: Animation: {"group": "run", "direction": "side"} ({"group": "idle"} for an undirected one) or {"id": "anm_..."}.

animation.description: "group/direction" of the animation owning it.

frameIndex.description: Frame index in the animation (the source's for a mirror).

target.description: "final" (whole composite) or the part layer name.

mirror.description: True for a mirror animation's own final override.

reason.description: "hash": the pixels under it changed; "no-target": nothing to compare with (hidden part, deleted frame); "error": it could not be rendered.

animation.description: "group/direction" of the animation owning it.

frameIndex.description: Frame index in the animation (the source's for a mirror).

target.description: "final" (whole composite) or the part layer name.

mirror.description: True for a mirror animation's own final override.

reason.description: "hash": the pixels under it changed; "no-target": nothing to compare with (hidden part, deleted frame); "error": it could not be rendered.

valid.description: Ids of the overrides that are up to date.

name: override_resolve
title: override.resolve
description:
Resolve overrides: "keep" them, "rebase" onto the current art, or "discard" them.

Name overrides by id (from override_list) or pass allStale: true. "keep" changes nothing (a stale override is still applied) and just confirms the ids exist. "rebase" accepts the art under the override as the new base, so it stops being stale; the frame must render. "discard" deletes the override and its pixels. With allStale, overrides that fail to render or have no target are left out of a rebase and listed in skipped. Check the frame with render_frame after a discard.

Edit: one undo step. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (Re-base every stale override after reviewing the render): {"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","action":"rebase","allStale":true}

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_create.

allStale.description: Also include every stale override of the document (default false).

resolved.description: Override ids the action applied to.

skipped.description: allStale rebase: ids left out because they fail to render or have no target.

name: part_paint_overlap
title: part.paintOverlap
description:
Close joint gaps by painting hidden overlap on the part drawn lower; the rest composite stays the same.

For each joint with gaps (rig_joint_check), paints only pixels the upper part covers at rest, growing the variant image and shifting its pivot to keep the part in place. One flat colour: the variant's most frequent opaque one, or color. At big bends it shows as a patch with no outline, so check the pose. "uncovered" lists joints no hidden paint can close; "skipped" joints with several parts per bone or a part rotated at rest. Run rig_joint_check next.

Edit: one undo step. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (Close the elbow gap of the hero): {"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","bones":["lower_arm_r"]}

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_create.

view.description: Rig view to check (default: the first view).

bones.description: Only joints whose child bone is one of these (default: all joints with gaps).

color.description: Paint colour: [r,g,b,a], or a palette index in an indexed document.

bones.description: Child bones of the joints it serves.

grew.description: Pixels the variant image grew on each side.

painted.description: Variants that were painted (empty when no joint has gaps).

uncovered.description: Joints with gap pixels no hidden paint can close.

name: part_paint_variant
title: part.paintVariant
description:
Paint a text grid into a part variant's own image.

"." transparent, "_" keeps. x, y are in the variant image; negative grows it (the pivot moves, the part stays put). Fixes a cut for every pose. Frame overrides of the part go stale (override_list). Locked palettes: palette colours only.

Edit: one undo step. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (Restore two forearm pixels): {"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","part":"lower_arm_r","x":0,"y":0,"rows":["11"],"legend":{"1":"#e8be96"}}

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_create.

part.description: Part: its part-layer name (e.g. "head"), part id ("prt_...") or layer id.

x.description: Column of the grid in the variant image (default 0).

changed.description: Pixels whose colour changed (0: nothing was written).

grew.description: Pixels the image grew on each side.

name: part_split
title: part.split
description:
Split a region (rect, lasso or flood) of a flat layer's cel into a new layer bound to a bone.

Fit the bones first: the part keeps the bone pivot of this moment. partName ("part:upper_arm_r") binds it, else overlap, else it stays a pixel layer. The part draws in every frame of every animation: key visible false (rig_set_pose) where other art shows. Refused: rig-block-order (a pixel layer covers the part), duplicate-variant (a second cut into one part: undo, recut it whole).

Edit: one undo step. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (Cut the head rectangle of a flat run frame into the head part): {"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","layer":"body","animation":{"group":"run"},"frame":0,"selection":{"kind":"rect","x":24,"y":16,"w":18,"h":12},"partName":"part:head"}

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_create.

layer.description: The flat pixel layer to cut from (id or name).

animation.description: Animation: {"group": "run", "direction": "side"} ({"group": "idle"} for an undirected one) or {"id": "anm_..."}.

frame.description: The frame whose cel is cut.

points.description: Closed polygon through canvas pixels [[x, y], ...] (the last joins the first).

boundary.description: Colours ([r,g,b,a], or palette indices) that stop the flood; default: only the seed colour.

includeBoundary.description: Also take the boundary-coloured pixels touching the region (an outline).

partName.description: Bind as "part:<bone>[.<part>][@variant][#view]" or a bone name.

name.description: Name of the new layer while it is not a part (default "split").

bind.description: Without partName: try to bind by overlap (default true).

view.description: View for names without #view and for overlap (default: the first).

zByBone.description: Default z of the new part by part-layer name, then bone name; higher draws on top. Set at creation; change later with rig_set_part_z.

layer.description: Layer holding the moved pixels (the part layer once bound).

image.description: Image id of the moved pixels.

bounds.description: Canvas rectangle of the moved pixels.

bound.description: Present when the layer became (part of) a part.

merged.description: True when folded into an existing part as a variant.

ambiguous.description: Bones tied for the overlap (nothing bound).

unlinked.description: Other frames whose linked cel now owns the original drawing.

name: pixels_read_grid
title: pixels.readGrid
description:
Read a region (at most 64x64 px) of a frame as a text grid: one symbol per pixel, "." transparent, with a legend of the colours present.

Without "layer" the region is the rendered frame (what pixels_write_grid edits on a rig frame); with a pixel "layer" it is that cel. Symbols 0-9A-Za-z are assigned by first appearance and valid for this call only; at most 62 colours (else read less). "rulers" adds column and row numbers, about 2 characters per pixel in all: read only the area you need. Feed `rows` and `legend` to pixels_write_grid.

Read-only. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (Read the hero head, 8x6 px at (21, 0)): {"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","animation":{"group":"default"},"frame":0,"x":21,"y":0,"width":8,"height":6}

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_create.

animation.description: Animation: {"group": "run", "direction": "side"} ({"group": "idle"} for an undirected one) or {"id": "anm_..."}.

layer.description: Read this pixel layer's cel instead of the rendered frame (mirror animations: not allowed).

x.description: Left column of the region, canvas px (default 0).

y.description: Top row of the region, canvas px (default 0).

width.description: Region width, 1..64 px (default: to the right edge, if at most 64).

height.description: Region height, 1..64 px (default: to the bottom edge, if at most 64).

rulers.description: Also return `ruled`: the rows with column and row numbers (default false).

animation.description: "group/direction" of the animation read.

source.description: "render": the rendered frame; "cel": one layer's cel.

x.description: Left column of the region, canvas px.

y.description: Top row of the region, canvas px.

legend.description: Symbol to colour "#rrggbb" ("#rrggbbaa" when translucent), for this call only. "." (transparent) is not listed.

rows.description: One string per pixel row, `width` symbols each.

ruled.description: Only with rulers: two header lines of column numbers, then each row prefixed by its row number.

name: pixels_write_grid
title: pixels.writeGrid
description:
Paint a text grid (at most 32x32 px) at (x, y) of a frame; symbols come from "legend".

"." writes transparent, "_" keeps the pixel. On a rig omit layer: differences from the rendered frame become overrides of this frame only. They are for touch-ups of a few pixels: art pasted over a pose is not rig animation and goes stale when the pose changes. If the rig cannot show something, say so instead. A part layer is refused. On flat art name the pixel `layer`. Locked palettes only take palette colours.

Edit: one undo step. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (Move the hero's eye one pixel left (an override on the head)): {"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","animation":{"group":"default"},"frame":0,"x":26,"y":4,"rows":["21"],"legend":{"1":"#e8be96","2":"#1e1e28"}}

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_create.

animation.description: Animation: {"group": "run", "direction": "side"} ({"group": "idle"} for an undirected one) or {"id": "anm_..."}.

layer.description: Pixel layer whose cel to write. Omit on a rig frame (the rendered frame is edited into overrides), or when the document has exactly one pixel layer.

x.description: Canvas column of the grid's left edge (default 0).

y.description: Canvas row of the grid's top edge (default 0).

rows.description: Pixel rows, at most 32 rows of at most 32 equally long symbols: "." transparent, "_" keep, 0-9A-Za-z from the legend.

legend.description: Symbol (one of 0-9A-Za-z) to colour "#rrggbb" or "#rrggbbaa". Only symbols used in `rows` need an entry.

animation.description: "group/direction" of the animation written.

target.description: "overrides": rig frame, edits stored as overrides; "cel": a pixel layer cel was rewritten.

changed.description: Pixels whose colour changed (0: nothing was written).

layer.description: Name of the layer written; only for target "cel".

overrides.description: Ids of the overrides created, in order; empty unless target is "overrides".

newlyStale.description: Ids of earlier overrides this edit made stale (still applied; re-base or discard them).

name: pxf_pack
title: pxf.pack
description:
Build a .pxf from a .pxfd folder (the inverse of pxf_unpack).

Packs manifest.json, document.json, images/ and render/ of the folder; .gdignore and other files are ignored. The archive is built by the same deterministic writer as a save, atomically, replacing an existing file. file defaults to the folder name with .pxf. Works on files, not on open documents: doc_open the result to validate it.

File I/O. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (Rebuild hero.pxf from its folder): {"dir":"/work/hero.pxfd"}

dir.description: The .pxfd folder (absolute, inside the workspace roots).

file.description: The .pxf to write, named *.pxf (default: beside the folder).

name: pxf_unpack
title: pxf.unpack
description:
Expand a .pxf into a .pxfd folder (manifest, document, images, render cache).

Writes one file per archive entry (bytes verbatim) plus an empty .gdignore so Godot ignores the PNGs; the folder diffs well in git. dir defaults to the file name with .pxfd. An existing folder is refused unless overwrite is true (only a folder named *.pxfd is ever replaced). Works on the file, not on an open document: doc_save first. pxf_pack is the inverse.

File I/O. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (Expand hero.pxf next to itself): {"file":"/work/hero.pxf"}

file.description: The .pxf to expand (absolute, inside the workspace roots).

dir.description: Folder to create, named *.pxfd (default: beside the file).

name: render_contact_sheet
title: render.contactSheet
description:
Render the frames of some or all animations as one labelled PNG contact sheet (long edge at most 1568 px), optionally with bone lines and pivot markers.

Judge motion across frames (before/after a re-pose, a walk cycle): vision judges gesture and readability, lint owns precision (1 px gaps, off-palette pixels). Check the tile edges: art past the canvas is cut off and lint does not report it. Tiles are labelled "GROUP/DIRECTION #n" (n = frame index). The scale is the largest that fits 1568 px, or lower than `scale`. `bones` draws yellow bone lines and `pivots` red pivot squares (need a rig).

Read-only. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (Show every frame of the hero with the skeleton drawn): {"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","bones":true,"pivots":true}

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_create.

animations.description: Animations to show, in order (default: all).

items.description: Animation: {"group": "run", "direction": "side"} ({"group": "idle"} for an undirected one) or {"id": "anm_..."}.

scale.description: Integer upscale to start from, 1..16 (default: the largest that fits 1568 px; reduced until it fits).

skin.description: Skin name or id ("skn_..."); omit for the base render.

bones.description: Draw a line from each bone pivot to its tip on every tile (default false).

pivots.description: Draw a marker on each bone pivot pixel on every tile (default false).

frames.description: Number of frames on the sheet.

data.description: The PNG file, base64 (standard alphabet, padded).

name: render_frame
title: render.frame
description:
Render one frame to an upscaled PNG on a checkerboard (long edge at most 1568 px), optionally with bone lines and pivot markers.

Look at the result of an edit: vision judges gesture, proportions and readability, lint owns precision (1 px gaps, off-palette pixels). `bones` draws a yellow line from each bone pivot to its tip, `pivots` a red square on each pivot pixel (both need a rig). With either, `output.bones` lists pivots and tips as canvas numbers: how to read a posed skeleton. Transparent pixels show a grey checkerboard.

Read-only. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (Look at frame 0 of the hero with the skeleton drawn): {"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","animation":{"group":"default"},"frame":0,"scale":8,"bones":true,"pivots":true}

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_create.

animation.description: Animation: {"group": "run", "direction": "side"} ({"group": "idle"} for an undirected one) or {"id": "anm_..."}.

scale.description: Integer upscale 1..16 (default and maximum: the largest that keeps the long edge within 1568 px).

skin.description: Skin name or id ("skn_..."); omit for the base render.

bones.description: Draw a line from each bone pivot to its tip (default false).

pivots.description: Draw a marker on each bone pivot pixel (default false).

animation.description: "group/direction" of the rendered animation.

scale.description: The upscale used (may be lower than requested to fit 1568 px).

data.description: The PNG file, base64 (standard alphabet, padded).

bones.description: The overlay bones in canvas pixels; present when bones or pivots was set.

parent.description: Parent bone name; missing for a root bone.

pivot.description: Snapped pivot pixel [x, y], canvas coordinates.

tip.description: Bone tip [x, y]: the pivot plus the bone length along its world direction.

name: rig_apply_template
title: rig.applyTemplate
description:
Apply a humanoid skeleton template: bones matched by name are reused, missing ones are created.

Templates: humanoid-side (view "side"), humanoid-front ("front"), humanoid-back ("back"). Without view a new view is created (named after the template, or viewName); with view the rest pose is set there. The template origin is the document origin. Rest: pelvis -90 (up), limbs 180 relative to it (down). Proportions are generic: compare with render_frame (bones) and refit with rig_edit_bones before any part_split. Bones that exist with another parent are refused.

Edit: one undo step. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (Set the rest pose of the hero in its existing side view): {"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","template":"humanoid-side","view":"side"}

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_create.

template.description: Skeleton template: humanoid-side, humanoid-front or humanoid-back.

height.description: Character height in px, feet row to top of head (default 48).

view.description: Existing view to set the rest pose in (default: a new view).

viewName.description: Name of the new view (default: the template name, e.g. "side"); ignored with view.

viewId.description: Id of the view the template was applied to.

bones.description: Bone id per template bone name (reused and created).

created.description: Names of the bones that were created.

name: rig_bake
title: rig.bake
description:
Bake a rig animation into one plain pixel layer: as a new animation, or in place.

Renders every frame (parts, overrides, post-passes, exported layers) into a pixel layer "baked" and hides the parts. mode "new" adds animation <group>_baked; "replace" bakes in place. A mirror cannot be baked: bake its source. Baked pixels no longer follow the rig.

Destructive: pass "confirm": true. One undo step. mode "replace" drops the animation's keys, overrides and post-passes and merges other exported layers (undo restores it); "new" only adds an animation and a layer. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (Bake the hero idle as a new animation): {"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","animation":{"group":"default"},"mode":"new","confirm":true}

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_create.

animation.description: Animation: {"group": "run", "direction": "side"} ({"group": "idle"} for an undirected one) or {"id": "anm_..."}.

mode.description: "new" keeps the source; "replace" bakes it in place.

name.description: mode "new": group of the baked animation (default <group>_baked).

confirm.description: Must be true: this operation is destructive.

animation.description: Id of the baked animation.

layer.description: Id of the new pixel layer holding the baked pixels.

frames.description: Frame ids of the baked animation, in play order.

cels.description: Cels of other exported pixel layers consumed at the baked frames.

dropped.description: What a "replace" bake removed (all zero for "new").

name: rig_bind_parts
title: rig.bindParts
description:
Bind pixel layers to bones as parts, by layer name ("part:<bone>[.<part>][@variant][#view]") or by overlap.

By name: a layer called part:upper_arm_r (or just a bone name) becomes that bone's part; @variant adds a variant of the same part, #view another view. By overlap: remaining layers bind to the bone their opaque pixels cover, only with a clear winner (ties are listed as ambiguous). The part keeps the bone pivot of this moment: fit the bones first. Animated and translucent layers are skipped. Running it again changes nothing. Cut flat art with part_split.

Edit: one undo step. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (Bind every layer named after a bone, no overlap guessing): {"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","byOverlap":false}

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_create.

layers.description: Only these layers (default: every pixel layer).

byOverlap.description: Bind the rest by overlap with the bones (default true).

rawNames.description: Source names to parse instead of layer names, by layer: {"arm": "part:upper_arm_r@open#side"}.

view.description: View for names without #view and for overlap (default: the first).

zByBone.description: Default z of new parts by part-layer name, then bone name; higher draws on top. Set at creation; change later with rig_set_part_z.

merged.description: True when folded into an existing part as a variant.

bound.description: Layers that became (part of) a part.

ambiguous.description: Layers whose overlap has no clear winner (left alone).

skipped.description: Layers left alone, with the reason.

name: rig_edit_bones
title: rig.editBones
description:
Edit the skeleton: add/delete/reparent/rename bones, set length and rest pose per view, add/rename/delete views.

Edits run in order; one failure undoes all. A bone with parts or (without cascade) children cannot be deleted. Rest x/y: root = canvas pivot, child = canvas offset from the parent pivot. Rest angle adds to the parent's: world 0 = +x, 90 = down, so a thigh pointing down under a pelvis at -90 is 180. Returns no geometry: check with render_frame (bones).

Edit: one undo step. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (Fit a thigh: 2 px left of the pelvis pivot, pointing down): {"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","edits":[{"action":"setRest","bone":"thigh_l","view":"side","x":-2,"y":0,"angle":180},{"action":"setLength","bone":"thigh_l","length":8}]}

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_create.

rest.description: Rest pose in one view (without it the bone is unused in every view).

x.description: Root: canvas pivot x. Child: canvas offset x from the parent pivot, px.

y.description: Root: canvas pivot y. Child: canvas offset y from the parent pivot, px.

angle.description: Added to the parent's world angle, deg clockwise; world 0 = +x, 90 = down, -90 = up.

cascade.description: Also delete all descendants (default: refused when it has children).

parent.description: New parent, or null to make it a root. The art stays put.

x.description: Root: canvas pivot x. Child: canvas offset x from the parent pivot, px.

y.description: Root: canvas pivot y. Child: canvas offset y from the parent pivot, px.

angle.description: Added to the parent's world angle, deg clockwise; world 0 = +x, 90 = down, -90 = up.

directions.description: Directions it draws (each in one view only).

id.description: Id of the bone or view the edit created.

results.description: One entry per edit, in order.

name: rig_fit_pose
title: rig.fitPose
description:
Find the bone angles (deg, relative to rest) and part variants whose render of one frame matches a target image.

Target: file (PNG, canvas size) or targetFrame. Searches each bone angle within ±range and each listed part variant. Pass the output bones and parts to rig_set_pose to apply them. exact: no pixel differs; else error counts them. Seeded: the same input gives the same result. A miss is not proof that no pose fits: raise maxRenders or narrow range.

File I/O. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (Pose the right arm like a reference image): {"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","animation":{"group":"default"},"frame":0,"file":"/work/reference.png","bones":["upper_arm_r","lower_arm_r"],"parts":["lower_arm_r"]}

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_create.

animation.description: Animation: {"group": "run", "direction": "side"} ({"group": "idle"} for an undirected one) or {"id": "anm_..."}.

frame.description: The frame to pose; its other keys stay as they are.

file.description: Target PNG, the size of the canvas.

targetFrame.description: Target: another frame of this animation, rendered.

bones.description: Bones whose angle to search (names or ids; default: every bone).

parts.description: Parts whose variant to search (default: none).

range.description: Search each angle within ±range deg of rest (default 180).

animation.description: "group/direction" of the animation.

exact.description: True when the render equals the target (error 0).

error.description: Pixels that differ from the target at the best pose.

bones.description: Best angle by bone name: the bones input of rig_set_pose.

parts.description: Best variant by part name: the parts input of rig_set_pose.

name: rig_fit_template
title: rig.fitTemplate
description:
Fit a humanoid template to landmark points: lengths and rest pose in one call.

Like rig_apply_template, but sizes the bones from landmarks (canvas px, arms hanging): headTop, hips, feet (between the soles; becomes the root), optional handL/handR fingertips. Existing bones are resized. Check with render_frame (bones), then touch up with rig_edit_bones.

Edit: one undo step. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (Fit the side template to a 47 px character): {"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","template":"humanoid-side","view":"side","landmarks":{"headTop":{"x":31,"y":16},"hips":{"x":30,"y":44},"feet":{"x":30,"y":63},"handR":{"x":38,"y":47}}}

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_create.

hips.description: Hip joint (thigh pivot); between headTop and feet.

feet.description: Between the feet on the sole row: the root pivot.

handL.description: Fingertip of the left hand (+x in front view).

handR.description: Fingertip of the right hand; one hand serves both.

view.description: Existing view to set the rest pose in (default: new).

viewName.description: Name of the new view; ignored with view.

viewId.description: Id of the view the fit was written to.

created.description: Names of the bones that were created.

resized.description: Names of the existing bones whose length changed.

name: rig_joint_check
title: rig.jointCheck
description:
Sweep each joint of one rig view and report the pixel gaps that open on the outer side of a bend.

A rig passes when summary.gapCount is 0. The full output is about 400 characters per joint: pass compact for a short form, or use lint with enable ["rig.jointGap"] for pass or fail. The sweep moves one joint at a time, rangeDeg around rest (default 30): a pose beyond that is not checked, so look at the render. Fix gaps with part_paint_overlap, or by moving part pivots, then check again. Checks the view that draws the first direction of the given view (default: the first view).

Read-only. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (Check the first view of the hero): {"doc":"doc_g1ed5q"}

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_create.

view.description: Rig view to check (default: the first view).

rangeDeg.description: Sweep range, degrees either side of rest.

radius.description: Window radius of the check, px.

compact.description: Short form: summary and problems, no joints.

rangeDeg.description: Sweep range, degrees either side of rest.

radius.description: Window radius of the check, px.

joints.description: One entry per joint, sorted by bone name. Absent when compact.

gapCount.description: Gap pixels summed over the sweep.

union.description: Distinct gap pixels over the sweep, sorted by y then x.

problems.description: Joints with gaps. Only when compact.

gapCount.description: Gap pixels summed over the sweep.

name: rig_mirror_animation
title: rig.mirrorAnimation
description:
Add a mirror of an animation under a new direction: same group, flipped around the origin.

The mirror stores no frames or pixels: it plays the source flipped horizontally about the document origin (markers flip too, names stay), so later edits of the source carry over: pose the source, not the mirror. Asymmetric art needs a separate animation. The mirror takes the source's group and loop; the direction must be new for that group. A source cannot be a mirror itself. Final overrides of the mirror can be added with pixels_write_grid on it.

Edit: one undo step. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (Mirror the hero idle as its left-facing twin): {"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","source":{"group":"default"},"direction":"left"}

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_create.

source.description: The animation to mirror (an authored one, not itself a mirror).

direction.description: Direction of the mirror, e.g. "left" for a "right" source.

animation.description: Id of the new mirror animation.

name: rig_read_pose
title: rig.readPose
description:
Read one frame: bone and part values, and which are real keys (the rest are interpolated or held).

Output matches rig_set_pose input: pass bones and parts back unchanged. Lists only bones and channels that some frame keys; the rest are at rest. keyed names the real keys on this frame ("bones.<name>.<channel>"); other values are interpolated or held. Writing a value back makes it a key: this frame renders the same, other frames may change, so write back only what you mean to key. Mirror animations: read the source.

Read-only. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (Read frame 2 of the run cycle): {"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","animation":{"group":"run","direction":"side"},"frame":2}

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_create.

animation.description: Animation: {"group": "run", "direction": "side"} ({"group": "idle"} for an undirected one) or {"id": "anm_..."}.

bones.description: By bone name: angle, offset {x,y}, flipX, and interp of the stored key.

parts.description: By part name: variant name or "auto", z, visible.

name: rig_set_part_z
title: rig.setPartZ
description:
Set a part's default z (draw order) after creation.

Higher z draws on top (default 0). Replaces per-frame z keys of rig_set_pose. A frame z key still wins: keyedFrames counts them. rig_joint_check and part_paint_overlap use the new order.

Edit: one undo step. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (Draw the right forearm above the torso): {"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","part":"lower_arm_r","z":5}

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_create.

part.description: Part: its part-layer name (e.g. "head"), part id ("prt_...") or layer id.

keyedFrames.description: Frames with their own z key for this part.

name: rig_set_pivot
title: rig.setPivot
description:
Set a part variant's pivot: the pixel (int px, in the variant image) that sits on the bone pivot.

Binding already puts the pivot on the bone: use this to shift a part against its bone. Coordinates are in the variant image, origin top-left, pixel centre; the pivot may lie outside the image (a floating hand). It moves the part's art relative to the bone, so do not nudge it to clear joint gaps: use part_paint_overlap. Run rig_joint_check next. Variant names repeat across views: pass view when the name is ambiguous.

Edit: one undo step. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (Move the forearm pivot two pixels right): {"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","part":"lower_arm_r","pivot":{"x":3,"y":1}}

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_create.

part.description: Part: its part-layer name (e.g. "head"), part id ("prt_...") or layer id.

view.description: Resolve the variant name among this view's variants.

pivot.description: New pivot, int px in the variant image.

name: rig_set_pose
title: rig.setPose
description:
Set bone keys (angle deg clockwise, offset int px) and/or part keys (variant, z, visible) on one frame or many.

Channels you pass replace the stored ones; null removes a bone or part key. A channel with no key here interpolates between keys on other frames, not back to rest: key offsets on every frame or on none. Part keys hold both ways: set z or visible once. "frames" poses many frames as one undo step. Output keyed lists bones keyed; interpolated, bones keyed elsewhere but not on a posed frame (keyAll keys them at rest). Art past the canvas edge is cut off. Next: render_contact_sheet.

Edit: one undo step. Conventions: origin top-left, y down, angles deg clockwise, integer px.

Example (Raise the right arm on frame 0): {"doc":"doc_g1ed5q","animation":{"group":"default"},"frame":0,"bones":{"upper_arm_r":{"angle":-45},"lower_arm_r":{"angle":-30}}}

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_create.

animation.description: Animation: {"group": "run", "direction": "side"} ({"group": "idle"} for an undirected one) or {"id": "anm_..."}.

bones.description: Bone keys by bone name (or id); null removes the key.

angle.description: Degrees clockwise from rest; child bones follow (FK).

offset.description: Pivot shift from rest, integer px.

flipX.description: Mirror the bone horizontally about its pivot.

parts.description: Part keys by part-layer name (or part id); null removes the key.

variant.description: Variant name or id, or "auto" (FR-RIG-14); holds until the next key.

z.description: Draw order, held until the next key; higher on top (default: the view's).

visible.description: Show or hide the part from this frame on.

keyAll.description: Also key all other bones at rest on posed frames.

animation.description: "group/direction" of the posed animation.

frameIndex.description: The posed frame; the first with "frames".

changed.description: Keys that changed, as "bones.<name>" / "parts.<name>"; empty when nothing did.

interpolated.description: Bones that interpolate on a posed frame.
